title: Speciality Restaurants Ltd - 534425 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Speciality Restaurants Q4 FY26 revenue up 13.65% YoY and PAT up 44.20%, with SSG of 2.25% for the quarter and 11.57% in April.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue growth of 13.65% YoY and PAT growth of 44.20%, helped by 2.25% same-store sales growth and gross margin expansion from 69.1% to 70.4%. Full-year SSG was 1.49%, and April SSG reached 11.57%, which management attributed to higher dine-in covers and refurbishments of older restaurants. Management guided to about 15% top-line growth in FY27 and about 15-16% EBITDA growth on revenue, with 32 new outlets planned. On the cost side, the company took a 4% price increase and moved 78% of its kitchens off LPG/PNG to induction, targeting 100% within 20 days.

financial_highlights.metric: Profit after tax growth (Q4 FY26, YoY)

segments.name: Mainland China / Asia Kitchen / Gong (Asian brands)
segments.commentary: Mainland China AOV is INR 1,200-1,300 per cover; Asia Kitchen INR 1,000-1,100; Gong INR 2,500-3,000, with a Bandra launch and Pune and Delhi (Vasant Kunj) openings planned. Management sees Asia Kitchen and Mainland China reaching about 50 restaurants within 5 years.

segments.name: Haka (digital QSR, delivery-first)
segments.commentary: Haka operates from hybrid sites, with about 40-50% of new Mainland China stores co-locating a Haka and Oh! Calcutta cloud kitchen. Management expects Haka to reach a 'decent number' within two quarters; no figure was given.

segments.name: Walters and Sweet Bengal
segments.commentary: Walters AOV is about INR 700 and Sweet Bengal about INR 400 per cover. Plans include 15 new Walters (to 20 total) and 10 new Sweet Bengal outlets in FY27, with Sweet Bengal rebranding and FMCG packaging planned.

segments.name: Siciliana (Italian)
segments.commentary: Newer chain; management cited an average spend of about INR 1,200-1,300 per cover, equal to Mainland China, per the answer on Siciliana's pricing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of about 15%, implying revenue near INR 600 crores; management said 'maybe more' and suggested about INR 700 crores by FY28 at a slower pace.
EBITDA to grow about 15-16% for each percentage of revenue growth, as front-end costs of new restaurants weigh over the next 2 years.
Restaurant-level EBITDA of about 15% post-rent (22% pre-rent) for a 2,500-3,000 sq ft store generating INR 8-9 crores revenue; breakeven in 4-6 months.
FY27 capex of INR 40 crores for renovations and new stores; 8 new restaurants (INR 32 crores) and QSR/confectionery (about INR 5 crores) for a total of INR 37 crores.
Planned 32 new outlets in FY26-27 (8 restaurants, 15 Walters, 10 Sweet Bengal), taking touch points from 121 at 31 March to about 150 by year-end.
Management expects double-digit SSG going forward after renovations of older restaurants.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex of INR 40 crores for renovations and new store openings; INR 37 crores is earmarked for 8 new restaurants and QSR/confectionery.
Restaurant capex of INR 12,000-13,000 per sq ft for Mainland China and Asia Kitchen; lower for small Walters and Sweet Bengal stores.
Renovations started at Andheri West, then Pune and Bangalore; about 4 restaurants refreshed by April.
Walters commissary set up in Maharashtra, geared for 20-25 stores.
Induction conversion: about INR 1.12 crores spent on induction woks since 4 March; 78% of the restaurant chain off LPG/PNG, with 100% targeted within 20 days.
Average occupancy is about 2 times installed cover capacity on an average basis, according to management.
demand_pricing: April 2026 SSG of 11.57%; management said there was no sign of consumer slowdown as of late May, citing a planned redemption-coupon scheme (for example INR 200 or INR 150 off a INR 1,000 meal) launching at the end of May.
Price increase of 4% taken in FY26, with management stating it would not take more than 4% and is not seeking extra margin from price.
Management said there is no significant reduction in spend historically during high inflation or domestic shocks other than COVID, and none currently.
Franchisees: 11 earlier, 7 remaining, each paying 6% of revenue as royalty with no capex by the company; management said Indian partners need 'skin in the game'.
Competition: management sees Panda Express as a fast QSR format different from Mainland China, so no threat to the business.

qa_highlights.question: What were same-store sales growth for Q4 and FY26, and why is the company lagging peers like Barbeque Nation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 SSG was 2.25% and full-year FY26 was 1.49%. Management said April SSG was 11.57%, driven by more dine-in covers, and blamed slow growth on unrenovated restaurants, with refurbishments now under way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the restaurant-level economics for top brands?
qa_highlights.answer: For a 2,500-3,000 sq ft store, revenue is INR 8-9 crores a year with 22% restaurant EBITDA before rent. Rent is about 20-21% of revenue (revenue-share triggers at 17-18%), leaving about 15% post-rent EBITDA. Breakeven takes 4-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company managing LPG and fuel supply, and what does induction cost?
qa_highlights.answer: The company started the transition on 4 March and imported wok-based induction sets (around 300). It has 78% of the chain off fuel, targeting 100% in 20 days. Management said induction cost is the same or lower, with a 6% saving in a pilot restaurant from avoiding pilot-flame wastage.

qa_highlights.question: Why not focus on fewer brands, given that the bottom 8 brands contribute under 10% each?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed seven focus brands (Mainland China, Asia Kitchen, Haka, Gong, Siciliana, Walters, Sweet Bengal). Other brands are profitable and will not be shut, but no further expansion is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is a buyback under consideration, given the cash pile and the share price correction?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the question would be taken up by the Board and it was too early to say.

qa_highlights.question: How can FY26 cash flow (about INR 80 crores CFO less about INR 50 crores rent) reconcile with a 15% EBITDA margin claim?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the 15-16% figure is at restaurant level after rent. Cash-flow EBITDA is after corporate costs, which fell to about 4% of revenue from 6-7% as the company resumed expansion.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (fuel, energy, freight) with only a 4% price increase taken so far; management said it is not seeking extra margin from pricing.
Consumer wallet pressure on discretionary dining if inflation or geopolitical uncertainty deepens; management reports no current impact.
Same-store sales growth of 1.49% in FY26 is weak; the 11.57% April figure needs to be sustained through FY27.
Execution risk on 32 new outlets, Gong expansion in Pune and Delhi, and Haka scaling.
Corporate cost and new-store front-end costs may slow EBITDA growth to about 15-16% against revenue growth of about 15%.
Management's FY27 revenue of about INR 600 crores and FY28 of about INR 700 crores are forward-looking and dependent on macro conditions.
Gross margin and EBITDA reconciliation: an analyst said cash-flow-implied EBITDA margin was about 7-8%, against management's 15-16% restaurant-level figure; this gap was not fully resolved.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansion-focused on store roll-out, brand pipeline and the fuel transition, with a clear view that demand is holding. Less precise on consolidated margin and cash-flow reconciliation, and cautious on buyback and mixed on the SSG gap versus peers.
key_quotes: So as we talk, 78% of our whole restaurant chain that includes the new restaurant chain called Siciliana, that's Italian is now not run by fuel
So we are prepared to 78%. We are going to 100% in exactly 20 days.
The leader holds the price line. So we continue to believe in that right from the beginning, and we've not taken more than 4% at this point.
